set.note: The ark had been at Kiriath-jearim twenty years (1 Samuel 7:2). Shen and Beth-car are unknown sites.

steps.label: Gathered to pray
steps.copy: “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.” They fast and confess their sin.

steps.label: Crying to the Lord
steps.copy: As the Philistines come up, Samuel offers a lamb and cries out, and the Lord answers him.

steps.label: Thunder from heaven
steps.copy: The Lord thunders against the Philistines, and Israel chases them from Mizpah to below Beth-car.

steps.label: The Ebenezer stone
steps.copy: Samuel sets up a stone between Mizpah and Shen: “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”

set.note: Telaim and the city of Amalek are unknown sites and are placed approximately.

steps.label: Mustered at Telaim
steps.copy: Samuel gives Saul the Lord's command against Amalek, and Saul counts his army at Telaim.

steps.label: Lying in wait
steps.copy: He comes to the city of Amalek, waits in the valley, and strikes the Amalekites.

steps.label: Sparing the best
steps.copy: Saul spares King Agag and the best of the sheep and cattle.

steps.label: A monument at Carmel
steps.copy: The Lord regrets making Saul king. Saul sets up a monument for himself at Carmel.

steps.label: Obedience over sacrifice
steps.copy: At Gilgal, Samuel confronts him: “Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice.”

set.note: 1 Samuel 25:1 says David went down to the Wilderness of Paran (the Greek Old Testament reads Maon). His men had been guarding Nabal's shepherds near Carmel (25:15-16).

steps.label: Nabal's insult
steps.copy: David sends ten young men to Nabal, who is shearing his sheep at Carmel. Nabal insults them.

steps.label: David's anger
steps.copy: “Strap on your swords!” About four hundred men follow David; two hundred stay with the supplies.

steps.label: Abigail's gift
steps.copy: Abigail loads donkeys with bread, wine and food and meets David in a mountain ravine.

steps.label: Bloodshed averted
steps.copy: David blesses her good sense for keeping him from avenging himself.

steps.label: Nabal dies
steps.copy: When Nabal hears what happened, his heart fails, and ten days later the Lord strikes him.

steps.label: Abigail marries David
steps.copy: David sends for her, and she goes with his messengers and becomes his wife.

steps.label: Defeat at Gilboa
steps.copy: Israel flees and falls on Mount Gilboa, and Saul's sons, Jonathan among them, are killed.

steps.label: Saul's end
steps.copy: Badly wounded by archers, Saul takes his own sword and falls on it.

steps.label: Hung at Beth-shan
steps.copy: The Philistines fasten his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

steps.label: A brave rescue
steps.copy: The valiant men of Jabesh-gilead journey all night and take down the bodies.

steps.label: Buried at Jabesh
steps.copy: They bury the bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh and fast seven days.

set.note: The text doesn't say where Abner brought Ish-bosheth from.

steps.label: Taken to Mahanaim
steps.copy: Abner brings Saul's son Ish-bosheth over to Mahanaim.

steps.label: Crowned over Israel
steps.copy: Abner makes him king over Gilead, Ephraim, Benjamin and all Israel; Judah follows David.

steps.label: Out to Gibeon
steps.copy: Abner marches out to Gibeon. Joab's men meet them across the pool, and a fierce battle follows.

steps.label: Asahel falls
steps.copy: Swift Asahel chases Abner and will not turn aside, and Abner kills him.

steps.label: Back through the night
steps.copy: All night Abner's men march through the Arabah, cross the Jordan and reach Mahanaim.

steps.label: The Philistines spread out
steps.copy: Hearing David is king, the Philistines spread out in the Valley of Rephaim. David asks the Lord.

steps.label: Burst of waters
steps.copy: At Baal-perazim: “Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me.”

steps.label: Circle behind them
steps.copy: When they come again, the Lord says to circle behind them and wait for the sound of marching in the balsam trees.

steps.label: Gibeon to Gezer
steps.copy: David does as the Lord commands and strikes the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.

steps.label: Bones from Jabesh
steps.copy: David takes the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had taken them from Beth-shan.

steps.label: Brought up
steps.copy: He brings them up, and the bones of the seven who were hanged are gathered too.

steps.label: Buried at Zela
steps.copy: They bury Saul and Jonathan in the tomb of Saul's father Kish.

steps.label: God answers
steps.copy: After that, God answers their prayers for the land.

set.note: Ophir's location is unknown; suggestions include southern Arabia, East Africa and India. The trail only points down the Red Sea.

steps.label: A fleet at Ezion-geber
steps.copy: Solomon builds a fleet at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

steps.label: Hiram's sailors
steps.copy: Hiram sends sailors who know the sea to serve with Solomon's men.

steps.label: Gold from Ophir
steps.copy: They sail to Ophir and bring back 420 talents of gold.

steps.label: Every three years
steps.copy: Once every three years the ships of Tarshish arrive with gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

steps.label: Two golden calves
steps.copy: “Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”

steps.label: One at Bethel
steps.copy: He sets up one calf at Bethel.

steps.label: One at Dan
steps.copy: The other goes to Dan, and the people go as far as Dan to worship it. This becomes a sin.

steps.label: A feast of his own
steps.copy: Jeroboam makes up a feast and offers sacrifices on the altar he built at Bethel.

set.note: The man of God's town in Judah isn't named.

steps.label: Sent to Bethel
steps.copy: As Jeroboam stands by the altar, a man of God comes from Judah to Bethel by the word of the Lord.

steps.label: Crying against the altar
steps.copy: “O altar, O altar … A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David.”

steps.label: The withered hand
steps.copy: Jeroboam's outstretched hand shrivels, the altar splits, and at the prophet's prayer the hand is restored.

steps.label: A lying invitation
steps.copy: An old prophet of Bethel deceives him into eating and drinking there, against the Lord's command.

steps.label: The lion on the road
steps.copy: As he goes on his way, a lion meets him and kills him; the donkey and the lion stand beside the body.

steps.label: By way of Edom
steps.copy: The kings of Israel, Judah and Edom take the long road through the Desert of Edom; after seven days they have no water.

steps.label: Ditches in the valley
steps.copy: Elisha: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’”

steps.label: Water from Edom
steps.copy: In the morning water flows from the direction of Edom, and the Moabites see it red as blood.

steps.label: Siege of Kir-hareseth
steps.copy: Israel routs Moab, destroys its cities and surrounds Kir-hareseth.

steps.label: Withdrawal
steps.copy: The king of Moab offers his firstborn son on the city wall. Great fury comes against Israel, and they go home.

steps.label: Coming to Damascus
steps.copy: Elisha comes to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram is sick.

steps.label: Hazael's gift
steps.copy: Hazael brings forty camel loads of gifts to ask whether the king will recover.

steps.label: The prophet weeps
steps.copy: Elisha stares at him until Hazael is ashamed, then weeps over the harm he will do Israel.

steps.label: A king foretold
steps.copy: “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.”

steps.label: Hazael takes the throne
steps.copy: The next day Hazael smothers the king and reigns in his place.

steps.label: Appeal to Assyria
steps.copy: “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me.” Ahaz sends the temple silver and gold.

steps.label: Damascus falls
steps.copy: The king of Assyria captures Damascus and carries its people into exile.

steps.label: A king's visit
steps.copy: Ahaz goes to meet Tiglath-pileser at Damascus and sees the altar there.

steps.label: A copied altar
steps.copy: He sends its design home, and Uriah the priest builds a copy for the temple in Jerusalem.

set.note: Gozan on the Habor River is shown; Halah and the cities of the Medes lay farther east.

steps.label: Three-year siege
steps.copy: The king of Assyria invades the land and besieges Samaria for three years.

steps.label: Carried to Assyria
steps.copy: Samaria falls, and Israel is settled in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

steps.label: Why it happened
steps.copy: Israel had sinned against the Lord and would not listen to the prophets, so they were exiled from their land.

set.note: Amos was one of the shepherds of Tekoa (Amos 1:1).

steps.label: Accused at Bethel
steps.copy: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, sends word to King Jeroboam that Amos is conspiring against him.

steps.label: “Flee to the land of Judah”
steps.copy: “Go away, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there.”

steps.label: No prophet by trade
steps.copy: “I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.”

steps.label: Sent by the Lord
steps.copy: “The LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’”

set.note: The Hebrew is Perath, normally the Euphrates, about 400 miles away. Some suggest a spring called Ein Prat (Wadi Farah), a few miles from Jeremiah's home town of Anathoth.

points.modern: the Euphrates (some suggest Ein Prat near Anathoth)

steps.label: Hide it at Perath
steps.copy: “Take the loincloth … go at once to Perath and hide it there in a crevice of the rocks.”

steps.label: Hidden as told
steps.copy: Jeremiah goes and hides it at Perath.

steps.label: Go back for it
steps.copy: Many days later: “Arise, go to Perath, and get the loincloth.”

steps.label: Ruined
steps.copy: He digs it up, ruined and of no use. So the Lord will ruin the pride of Judah and Jerusalem.

set.note: The road isn't recorded; by the usual route up the Tigris and around the desert it was roughly 1,000 miles.

steps.label: The sad cupbearer
steps.copy: Nehemiah serves wine to King Artaxerxes with a sad face. He prays, then answers.

steps.label: A bold request
steps.copy: “Send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so that I may rebuild it.” The king grants it.

steps.label: Arrival in Jerusalem
steps.copy: With army officers and horsemen, he delivers the king's letters beyond the Euphrates and reaches Jerusalem.

steps.label: Inspecting by night
steps.copy: He rides out at night to inspect the broken walls, then tells the people: “Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem.”

steps.label: Number the people
steps.copy: “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops.” Joab objects but goes.

steps.label: Starting at Aroer
steps.copy: They cross the Jordan and camp near Aroer, in the middle of the valley.

steps.label: Gad, Jazer and Gilead
steps.copy: They go on toward Gad and Jazer, then to Gilead.

steps.label: On to Dan
steps.copy: Through Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, on to Dan-jaan.

steps.label: Around to Sidon
steps.copy: They reach Sidon on the coast.

steps.label: The fortress of Tyre
steps.copy: They go toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites.

steps.label: Down to Beersheba
steps.copy: Finally they go to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.

steps.label: Back to Jerusalem
steps.copy: After nine months and twenty days they return to Jerusalem with the count.

set.note: The Ascent of Ziz and the Wilderness of Jeruel are unknown; they lay between En-gedi and Tekoa.

steps.label: A vast army
steps.copy: Word comes that a vast army from beyond the Sea is already at En-gedi. Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast.

steps.label: Not your battle
steps.copy: “The battle does not belong to you, but to God.” Tomorrow they will see the enemy coming up the Ascent of Ziz.

steps.label: Singers go first
steps.copy: Early in the morning they leave for the Wilderness of Tekoa, with singers praising the Lord ahead of the army.

steps.label: The enemy turns on itself
steps.copy: As they sing, the Lord sets ambushes, and the invaders destroy one another.

steps.label: The Valley of Blessing
steps.copy: On the fourth day they gather to bless the Lord, and the place is named the Valley of Beracah.

steps.label: Home with joy
steps.copy: With Jehoshaphat at their head, they return joyfully to Jerusalem.
